I've been farming this land for over thirty years, same as my mother before me. I know this soil. I know the rains. I don't need a book to tell me what grows here.

In Quzhou, everyone grows wheat in the winter and corn in the summer. That's what the land is suited for. That's what the grain buyers in town want. My 6 mu gets split — 5 mu for the wheat-corn rotation, and 1 mu near the house where I grow vegetables for eating.

For wheat, I'll buy the improved seed from the village seed shop — the same kind I bought last year, worked fine. I'll rotary-till after the corn comes off in September, then put down compound fertilizer before planting and do a top-dress of urea in spring when the plants joint. I water three times: once before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide early, one spray for aphids and rust in April.

For corn, I direct-seed into the wheat stubble right after harvest in June. No tilling needed. I use hybrid seed, the kind they sell in the market, everyone uses it, yields are good. I put fertilizer down at planting and side-dress when it's knee-high. Water twice if summer rain is short. Spray herbicide once, check for corn borer later.

I'm not trying anything new this year. I'm 55, my back is not what it was, and new ideas cost money I may not get back.
